1000	Onward, and this is also the aspect of the side

1001	of the talmid chacham within me.

1002	That is, to whom must I reveal my shortcomings and my flaws?

1003	By virtue of what, and to whom?

1004	By virtue of the talmid chacham.

1005	What is a talmid chacham?

1006	The Rabbi says that the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "Chacham," since He gives the light of wisdom.

1007	He bestows the light of wisdom.

1008	So a talmid chacham is one who emulates the Creator and becomes a giver like Him.

1009	But the Holy One, blessed be He, does not give only through an external act, but from

1010	His inwardness.

1011	What is meant by His inwardness?

1012	That is, does the Creator have an inside and an outside?

1013	No, we are speaking from our own perception.

1014	That is, from the pure form of giving.

1015	A form within a form.

1016	This is the highest thing we can grasp of Him, as beneficence:

1017	as an infinite desire to do good, complete with every perfection, without

1018	any lack.

1019	Keter of the Infinite, the thought of Creation, is the highest thing we can grasp.

1020	Therefore, if I confess before a talmid chacham, a judge, revealing my shortcomings and

1021	my flaws before the side and aspect of the talmid chacham, then I can repair.

1022	Otherwise I will fall into a matter of principle, or I will not want to reveal them.

1023	Why should I see my shortcomings?

1024	I have no interest at all in seeing my shortcomings.

1025	But if I am going to reveal them, then before a talmid chacham.

1026	Why?

1027	He will explain.

1028	But it says, "Take with you words."

1029	This is the confession of words.

1030	This is the aspect of malchut.

1031	Like "one word per generation."

1032	"Davar," an expression of a leader, a ruler.

1033	"And return to HaShem," that they repair and raise the words,

1034	that is, the aspect of malchut,

1035	the aspect of Elokim,

1036	which is judgment, "to HaShem," which is mercy, which is beneficence.

1037	That is, as above: in HaShem, "I will praise a word," in Elokim, "I will praise a word," that is, that he know that all his afflictions are entirely for his good,

1038	and bless over all things, "the Good and the Beneficent."

1039	That is, that he join chesed and gevurah, left and right, judgment and mercy.
